newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH - Budget bills update for Nov 27 - overview.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH - Budget bills update for Nov 27 - overview.

text.p: One major bill from the Australian budget has been through the wringer of amendment in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, and it was massacred.
There is no reason to expect the same treatment for all the other contentious budget bills, whose combined fiscal value exceeds A$1 billion in 1997/98, but it was hardly a good start.

The most notable aspect of the treatment of that bill, the Social Security (Newly Arrived Residents' Waiting Periods) Bill, was the Democrats' apparent failure to meet the government half way. The Labor Opposition, the Democrats and Greens minor parties and two Independents combined to protect immigrants' access to most social security, but not unemployment benefits.
On initial government reckoning, the budget lost about A$130 million a year from Tueday's amendments to the bill that would have excluded immigrants from social security for two years.

Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman's office estimated that the amendments cost about A$400 million in its first four years of operation, almost all of the A$550 million saving that the bill was supposed to create in that time.

Those estimates of the budget loss seemed too high, and Treasurer Peter Costello appears to have corrected them today: in Melbourne he told reporters the cost was A$200 million over the period of the forward estimates -- that is, the four years to June 2000.
His figure is remarkably close to Labor's estimate that the amendments cost about a third of the value of the bill.
Either way, the fiscal measure has suffered grievous damage.
The Senate has not actually passed it yet, only amended it (actually, requested an amendment, since it's a money bill, which the Senate is not allowed to change).
But presumably the government will take what it can get and the bill will go through in the form that the Senate demands.

The next budget bill will probably be the Higher Education Legislation Amendment Bill, whose contentious measures are worth about A$360 million in 1997/98. (See the accompanying report that gives greater detail on the budget bills.)
This bill will probably be dealt with on Thursday or Friday.
A background issue in all of this is when the government will ask the Senate to finish the Telstra privatisation bill, which will not be achieved in quick smart time.
The Senate is scheduled to finish its sittings for the year on December 13, a little over two weeks away.
